title: Employee Lifecycle Operating Manual (2023)
body:
Summary:
This manual walks through the employee lifecycle at Redwood Inference: sourcing and hiring, pre-boarding and the first week, role expectations and promotions, benefits and perks, tool access, lateral moves and offboarding. It is written for hiring managers, people-ops partners, new hires and engineering managers.

Purpose and scope:
- One practical reference covering process, templates, ownership and tooling across the lifecycle.
- Applies to US, EMEA and APAC hires unless a regional policy overrides a benefit or compliance rule.

Owners and escalation:
- Primary owner: People Ops (people-ops).
- Secondary owners: Hiring Managers (engineering/product) and IT & Security for provisioning.
- Escalation: People Ops -> Head of People Ops -> COO.

1) Hiring and candidate experience
Greenhouse is the system of record for candidates and scorecards. Use the standard loop so evaluations stay consistent.

Standard IC / engineering loop:
1. Recruiter screen (30 min): motivation, fit, logistics.
2. Technical screen (45 min): coding or system design by level.
3. Take-home or paired exercise where relevant.
4. Onsite loop (4–5 interviews, 60 min each): design, deep dive, product sense, manager, bar-raiser.
5. Debrief and decision.

Before the offer:
- Background checks scheduled where the role/region requires them.
- Compensation calibrated with People Ops and Finance.
- Offer drafted from the standard template (GH: /templates/offer-standard).
- Manager confirms the onboarding buddy and first-week plan.

Offers go out as Greenhouse PDFs with start date, manager, orientation details, first-week agenda, equipment plan and 30/60/90 expectations.

2) Pre-boarding (2–4 weeks before start)
- People Ops creates the Workday record, which triggers Okta provisioning.
- IT orders the laptop and peripherals; procurement SLA: 10 business days for US, 15 business days EMEA/APAC.
- Manager sends a welcome packet with agenda and buddy.
- New hire finishes security basics and code of conduct e-learning before day 1.

3) Day 1 and week 1
- Day 1: 09:30 welcome (People Ops), 10:30 accounts & SSO (IT), 13:00 team lunch, 15:00 product overview.
- Week 1: role-specific sessions, compliance training and a small starter task (<= 8 hrs).

Day 1 access checklist:
- Okta SSO working
- Email and Slack active
- Miro/Jira/Confluence permissions checked
- Github repo access and PAT guidance

4) Role expectations and career ladders
Every function keeps a leveled ladder with IC and manager tracks; managers share role rubrics at hiring and promotion time.

Promotion packet:
- Competency self-assessment
- 360 feedback via the People Ops template
- Evidence of impact (PRs, release notes, customer outcomes)
Evaluation criteria: scope increase, technical/functional depth, influence, and consistency over 6–12 months.

| Level | Scope | Expected outcomes | Promotion signal |
|-------|-------|-------------------|------------------|
| IC2   | Owns single feature | Delivers roadmap items, clear tickets | Reliable over 6 months |
| IC3   | Multi-feature / small service | Leads design, mentors, measurable KPIs | Moves a product metric |
| IC4   | Cross-team area | Shapes architecture, leads cross-team work | Recognized SME |

Managers complete Manager Essentials within 60 days of taking the role and review 30/60/90 plans monthly.

5) Benefits and perks
Benefits include health coverage, 401(k) or local equivalent, parental leave, flexible time off, a learning stipend, a home-office stipend and commuter benefits where applicable. Details are in Workday.

| Program | Eligibility | Notes |
|---------|-------------|-------|
| Health insurance | Full-time, post-probation | Several plans; enroll within 30 days |
| Parental leave | Full-time | 12 weeks primary, 6 weeks secondary (US policy) |
| Learning stipend | All employees | $1,000/year for conferences/courses |
| Home-office stipend | New hires | $500 one-time; ergonomic extras via People Ops |

Perks:
- Monthly wellness stipend (local currency)
- Quarterly hackday and offsite support
- Referral bonus paid after 60 days of hire

6) Internal tools
- HRIS: Workday (People Ops)
- ATS: Greenhouse (People Ops/Recruiting)
- SSO: Okta (IT/Security)
- Password manager: 1Password (IT/Security)
- Communication: Slack
- Code: Github Enterprise (Eng)
- Ticketing: Jira (Eng/Product)
- Docs: Confluence
- Cloud: GCP (Infra manages project namespaces)

Access requests:
1. Manager files a ServiceNow/IT portal ticket with role code and justification.
2. IT confirms procurement and assigns hardware.
3. Okta group sync grants tool access within 24 business hours (48 hours during hiring ramps).

Ticket template:
- Subject: "New hire access request: [Name] – [Team] – [Start Date]"
- Body: "Name: 
Role: 
Start date: 
Required groups: github:coder, jira:team-X, gcp:dev-project-A"

7) Lateral moves and sabbaticals
- Tell People Ops about a lateral move at least 30 days ahead of the target start.
- Sabbaticals: eligible after 3 years of continuous service; see the People Ops policy for approval.

8) Offboarding
1. Confirm the last day with payroll and benefits.
2. Knowledge transfer: a shadow week and written runbooks for critical duties.
3. Okta deprovisioning on the last day; rotate shared credentials.
4. People Ops schedules the exit interview.

Managers transfer ownership of customer accounts and keys before departure. Private deployment engineers' production credentials are rotated and reported to Security within 24 hours.

9) People Ops SLAs
- Full provisioning: 5 business days (US), 10 business days (EMEA/APAC).
- Offer-to-accept: median 7 days.
- 95% of hires complete the Day 1 access checklist by end of day.

10) Templates
30/60/90 outline:
- 30 days: learn the codebase, ship a small ticket, meet partners.
- 60 days: lead a small design, mentor, improve a CI/CD flow.
- 90 days: own a feature end-to-end with metrics.

Welcome Slack message:
"Please welcome @new-hire (Role, Team). Start date: 2024-03-04. Buddy: @buddy. First 1:1 with manager on Day 2. Say hi and share docs that will help them ramp."

FAQ:
Q: Who approves promotions?
A: Manager + peer review + People Ops calibration committee.
Q: How do I get a laptop upgrade?
A: Hardware request with manager approval; reviewed quarterly.

References
- Offer templates: /templates/offer-standard
- Promotion packet: /templates/promotion-packet
- Manager training: /learning/manager-essentials
- Security onboarding: /security/new-joiner

Revision history:
- 2023-06-12: created by Aisha Kapoor (People Ops)
- 2024-02-05: added benefits table and People Ops SLAs

Regional or legal policy takes precedence over this manual where they conflict. Questions: people-ops@redwood.com.
